newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: GOLF-HARWOOD EQUALS COURSE RECORD IN SOUTH AUSTRALIAN OPEN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-HARWOOD EQUALS COURSE RECORD IN SOUTH AUSTRALIAN OPEN.

text.p: Australian Mike Harwood equalled the course record on Friday when he shot a seven-under-par 65 to share the second round lead in the South Australian Open with New Zealand's Michael Long.
Long shot a 66 for a two-round total of 135 while an improved performance on the greens helped British Open champion Tom Lehman remain within sight of the leaders.
The world number two carded a 69 at the Kooyonga Golf Club to share fourth place on 137.
Shane Tait of Australia was second on 136 after a second round of 69 while Lehman was grouped with Australians Craig Parry, Gary Simpson, Matthew Goggin and Neil Kerry.
Lehman again struggled with his putter but felt he had improved on Thursday's first round of 68, when he said poor putting had cost him several shots.
The American however finished on an encouraging note with a birdie three on the 18th hole.
"I was stroking the ball well. If I keep going that way I should putt well over the next two days," Lehman said.
Former British Open champion Ian Baker-Finch's dreadful run continued, with the Australian missing the halfway cut after a disastrous second round of 78.
Baker-Finch appeared on course to make only his second cut in over two years until he made a double bogey six on his 16th hole after he drove his tee shot into a nest of ants.
The halfway cut was set at even-par 144, with Baker-Finch missing by five shots.
"I had a few bad breaks here and there. It all adds up," Baker-Finch said.
